# Rollback Drill Decision: Atlas Rehearsals

**Date:** 2026-07-02
**Participants:** Quinton Fairweather (CTO)

Quinton: "Atlas rollback rehearsals run monthly from now on. A rollback
we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have."

Key decisions:
- **Cadence**: monthly Atlas rollback rehearsals
- **Owner**: Quinton Fairweather

observations.why: Generalized conditional principle: any un-rehearsed rollback is framed as nonexistent, abstracting across all possible cases.

Naming the owner in a summary block is a settled, confident act of accountability — low arousal, positive valence.

positions.name: AtlasRehearsalDecisionRecord
positions.frame: What constitutes the settled record of an operational decision — the directive that establishes it, the cadence that names it, and the assignment that owns it?
positions.why: All three expressions share a calm-positive, decision-register performance: src-1 issues the standing directive, src-3 restates it as a bolded cadence label, src-4 names the accountable owner. Across affect, temporal, relational, power, and conviction reads they cluster together (legitimate authority, decision/authority-ranking regions, settled present/future concrete framing) as three facets of one act of ratifying and recording a policy — distinct from src-2's separately-marked aphoristic justification (principle/antithesis/alarm register), which stays apart.

placements.why: The document's whole content is about converting an assumed rollback capability into a demonstrated one via recurring rehearsal — a proof-of-capability concern. No existing strata category exists yet in this repo, and nothing supplied is even close, so this is minted standalone as the organizational home for readiness-proving content.
placements.title: operational readiness is demonstrated, not assumed
placements.frame: Does this content concern validating that a claimed operational capability actually exists through practiced demonstration?

placements.title: an unrehearsed capability is not a real capability
placements.frame: Is this expression treating rehearsal as the thing that makes a claimed capability actually exist, rather than as optional practice on top of an already-real capability?
placements.why: src-2's maxim states a general, reusable principle — that an un-rehearsed rollback is not actually held — which future envelopes about other unrehearsed capabilities will keep feeding; it names a subject, not a one-time fact, so it passes the narrative grain test and is placed under the newly-minted Proof strata as nothing existing captures this principle.

placements.title: rollback readiness becomes a standing, owned, recurring practice rather than a one-time claim
placements.frame: Does this expression establish or restate a recurring, owned operational cadence that converts a readiness principle into an ongoing practice?
placements.why: src-1 (directive), src-3 (cadence label), and src-4 (owner assignment) together record the operational instantiation of the readiness principle — a recurring monthly practice with a named accountable owner. This is a subject future envelopes will keep feeding (cadence changes, ownership handoffs, rehearsal outcomes), so it earns its own leaf rather than being folded as a fact into the principle leaf; placed as a specific instantiation under both the new Proof strata and the readiness-principle leaf just minted.
